chunks: It was said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): O Commander of the Faithful, inform us about "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" - is it from the Fatiha of the Book?
He said: Yes, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would recite it and count it as a verse from it, and he would say: The Fatiha of the Book is the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses.

key_terms.السبع المثاني: The Seven Oft-Repeated Verses, a Quranic term (15:87) identifying al-Fatiha
key_terms.فاتحة الكتاب: The Opening of the Book, referring to Surat al-Fatiha, the first chapter of the Quran

ai.seo_question: Is Bismillah a verse of Surat al-Fatiha according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) was asked whether the Basmala (Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim) is part of Surat al-Fatiha. He confirmed it is, stating that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to recite it and count it as one of its verses, and that al-Fatiha is the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses mentioned in Quran 15:87. This narration addresses a long-standing jurisprudential and exegetical debate among Muslims regarding the status of the Basmala in the opening chapter of the Quran.
